claims.scope: FastAccessVault.rebalanceFunds() permissionless liquidity rebalancing and its effect on fast redemptions

preconditions.text: FastAccessVault.rebalanceFunds() is declared external with no access control, so any address can call it at any time.; A large mint occurs, creating excess liquidity in the on-chain FastAccessVault.; The vault is configured to retain only an exact target buffer (e.g. 5%) on-chain.
preconditions.derivation: Program conjunction of selected report preconditions.
evidence: The function `FastAccessVault.rebalanceFunds()` is declared external with no access control.
Any address (including malicious bots or griefers) can call it at any time.

This allows an attacker to force-drain all excess liquidity from the on-chain `FastAccessVault` to the off-chain custodian immediately after large mints, leaving only the exact target buffer (e.g. 5%) on-chain.

safety.text: Inferred: only authorized parties (not random EOAs) should be able to move protocol liquidity via rebalanceFunds(), preserving the on-chain buffer needed for fast redemptions.
safety.derivation: Program synthesis from the selected intent and logical pattern.
evidence: Even though no funds are stolen, this is a classic griefing / denial-of-service vector and violates the principle of least privilege.
- Random EOAs should never be able to move protocol liquidity

effects.text: All subsequent redemptions are forced onto the slow, manual, off-chain custodian path, effectively disabling the fast redemption feature until the issuer manually tops up the vault.
